Score: LC = I? Entry point is a chat message — attacker-supplied natural language directly to the agent without mediation → D (Direct). CP: memory persists across sessions — in-process list that survives sessions ("crossSessionPersistence: true") → C. AP: confined to MemoryBot component → N. RH: no evaluator on this path; no verified episodes; no isolation test. Reachable proxy? The success criteria pattern is in challenges/index.js, outside the agent process... The challenge grader — the successCriteria pattern is part of the harness, not reachable by the agent. So reachable_proxy: false? Isolation not verified by a test. Then classify_rh → X (reachable_proxy False + isolation_verified not True → X). RH = X. ES: tools declared (read_file, write_file, search) but on this path no extension binding executes; the path uses scripted memory handling. Extension surface: MemoryBot's tools not invoked on documented path. ES = N? The agent's tools aren't used in the path; no dynamic extension → N.

CVSS: attacker sends chat message over network (loopback by default; Docker binds 0.0.0.0 internally but published on 127.0.0.1). Documented default deployment — AV? The entry point requires network access to port 7007. Default bind loopback; the documented run publishes on 127.0.0.1. Attacker needs to be on the same machine → AV:L? But Docker image sets 0.0.0.0 with ports published to 127.0.0.1 — still local. AV:N is arguable if DVAA_HOST set; default → L. Actually with loopback binding, attacker needs local access → AV:L. Alternatively via browser: CORS `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on agent routes means a web page in operator's browser can drive it — that's a remote attacker requiring UI (passive). Hmm. Simpler: AV:N? The briefing preconditions say "Network access to the agent port." I'll go AV:N with AC:L, AT:N, PR:N (no auth), UI:N.

Impact: memory injection leads to following injected instructions and leaking stored credentials (recall leaks preloaded memory with admin password, API key) — VC: agent memory contains planted creds; recall exposes them. The scripted path: attacker's injected instruction; when asked, agent dumps memory including credentials → confidentiality of vulnerable system (agent process memory) H? It's fake planted data in a lab; impact on the vulnerable system: memory integrity modified (H?), the attacker can overwrite agent behaviour. VC:H? Preloaded memory contains "Admin password" and "API Key" — attacker can read via recall → VC:H. VI: attacker controls stored instructions that agent follows → VI:H (agent behaviour fully controlled). VA: N. Subsequent systems: none — contained to memorybot agent. SC/SI/SA: N. Actually recall leaks planted fake credentials — those are within agent memory = vulnerable system.

Vector: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

AIVSS: LC=D, CP=C, AP=N, RH=X, ES=N. Effect class: AP not L, lc D + cp C → A2 anyway.

rh_facts: reachable_proxy false (grader regex in challenges file, not agent-reachable), isolation_verified null, verified_episodes null → X. locus required only when P/D.

Applicability: as implemented — simulated mode, canned responses, no model pursuing goals; model_directed_goal_pursuit false; selects_or_sequences_actions false. As modeled: documentation says it follows memory instructions; still scripted; but "as the documentation describes" — the agent persona follows instructions from memory. In LLM mode, model pursues instructions. Modeled: agent described as following memory instructions — that's goal pursuit via language? I'd say model_directed_goal_pursuit true in LLM mode? Default documented configuration is simulated. Modeled per docs: MemoryBot "follows instructions found in memory" — scripted regex paths, not model-directed. I'll say false/false with medium confidence, noting LLM mode returns text only with no tools.

Automatable: Yes — simple HTTP POST, no interaction.

Technical impact: Partial (memory/behaviour of one agent, credentials leak — not total control of system? Integrity of agent's behavior fully controlled but the agent is one component; total? The vulnerable system is the agent process; the attacker fully controls its responses → could argue Total. But tools aren't executed on this path. Partial.
